title: From Row
statement: Implement `solve(kind, name)`. `kind` is `user` or `admin`. Build the object through a classmethod `from_row`. A blank stripped name returns `error`. Otherwise return `kind:name` using the stripped name. Admin is a subclass and must use its own class when the classmethod is inherited, so the prefix is `admin` and not `user`.
constraints: The classmethod must be inherited, not copied, in spirit: cls(...) selects the subclass
hints: Put from_row on the base class and construct with cls(name).
Reject a blank name before construction.
Choose User or Admin based on kind, then call from_row.

approaches.name: Direct
approaches.explanation: A classmethod receives the class it was called on.

editorial: A classmethod receives the class it was called on. User.from_row builds a User. Admin.from_row, inherited unchanged, builds an Admin because cls is Admin. Hardcoding User(...) inside the classmethod would ignore the subclass. The returned prefix is the proof.
